irregularities.title: The live contest contains no stocks, but the brief asks to invest in highly volatile stocks
irregularities.detail: The permitted instrument list for The Leap by AMP Futures (September 2026) contains 94 instruments, every one of them a futures contract. There are zero NASDAQ, NYSE or AMEX single-stock contracts. A stocks-only strategy cannot be executed in the currently live edition.
irregularities.observed: 94 futures / 0 equities. Exchange breakdown: CBOT 17, CBOT_MINI 15, CME 24, CME_MINI 18, COMEX 5, COMEX_MINI 6, NYMEX 7, NYMEX_MINI 2.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: A tradeable universe of highly volatile stocks.
irregularities.resolution: Either target a future stocks edition (the 'Magnificent Seven' stocks edition of March 2026 completed with a winning return of only +17.58% — see TV-CONTEST-MAG7-MAR2026), or translate the volatility research into the futures universe. This session built data/volatile_stocks.json as the evidence base for what extreme stock volatility actually delivers, and the futures master list for what the live contest actually allows.

irregularities.title: Captured stock-edition champions are lower than captured futures champions; cause is untested
irregularities.detail: In the captured completed-champion sample, the two stocks editions returned +29.90% (1.299x) and +17.58% (1.1758x), while the maximum futures champion is 53.2072x. This is an observed association only. Edition balance, leverage, caps, symbol set, duration, and participant behavior differ, so the sample does not prove that asset class caused the gap.
irregularities.observed: completed stocks: best 1.299x (n=2); completed futures: best 53.2072x (n=5); small champion-only sample.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Stocks deliver 5x-100x.
irregularities.resolution: Keep the stocks module as historical reference, use only live-eligible futures for this edition, and do not infer a causal strategy from champion summaries.

irregularities.title: No 100x contest-account outcome is attested by the captured official sample
irregularities.detail: The brief sets a 100x target. Across the 16 sourced contest records, including one in-progress row, the maximum captured return multiple is 53.2072x (+5,220.72%). Zero captured records are at or above 100x. This is a statement about the captured TradingView sample, not a universal upper bound.
irregularities.observed: >=5x: 2 cases. >=10x: 2 cases. >=20x: 1 case. >=50x: 1 case. >=100x: 0 cases.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Verified 100x returns available.
irregularities.resolution: Treat 100x as an unverified contest target. Never describe 53.2072x as a ceiling; it is only the maximum in the captured sample.

irregularities.title: The maximum-return objective is still constrained by account survival and margin
irregularities.detail: This is a virtual-money competition, so real-money risk management is not the objective. However, at 20:1 leverage on a $250,000 balance, $5,000,000 is the maximum initial notional. A loss equal to 5% of that fully deployed notional is $250,000. The account cannot be reset, and TradingView documents margin-call behavior in its simulator. Survival and margin feasibility are therefore optimization constraints, not investor-protection advice.
irregularities.observed: balance 250,000; leverage 20:1; maximum initial notional 5,000,000; account reset prohibited.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Maximize simulated returns; real-money risk management is not the objective.
irregularities.resolution: Evaluate drawdown and margin calls only as feasibility diagnostics. Do not turn the project into a real-money risk-management plan.

irregularities.title: Partial locator scan initially misidentified SMCI's 2022 trough as the all-time low

A full-history monthly scan (2007 IPO onward) disproved it: monthly lows ran ≈ 0.44–0.51 (adjusted) in the 2008–2009 financial crisis. No all-time multiple was ever published from the partial scan; the verified SMCI record (22.66x) is explicitly window-bounded to the fetched 2022 trough window and 2024 peak window.

irregularities.resolution: Generate and audit the research autonomously. Label the Pine code as a backtest/forward-test artifact only and make no claim of competition-account automation.

irregularities.title: Market-data vendors block automated capture from datacenter IP ranges
irregularities.detail: Yahoo Finance returns HTTP 429 to every chart-API request made from the GitHub Actions runner range (both query1 and query2 hosts, confirmed by probe on 2026-09-17 with a browser User-Agent). Stooq returns a 795-byte JavaScript anti-bot challenge instead of CSV data. The capture pipeline therefore retries the identical vendor URLs through the public allorigins relay, a byte transport. Every relayed payload is validated against the expected vendor symbol and OHLC invariants and spot-verified against independent in-session captures; the transport used is recorded per symbol in data/market_history_index.json.
irregularities.observed: 20/20 symbols HTTP 429 direct from runner; stooq cl.f..eth.f all returned the identical 795-byte JS challenge; allorigins relay returned the full 27,505-byte CL=F 1-year JSON with valid chart structure.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Automated, reproducible ingestion of daily futures history from a free vendor.
irregularities.resolution: Open. The relay works but is a third-party dependency; a licensed feed (e.g. CME settlement-based continuous series) or a residential-IP capture remains the clean fix. Workflow probe annotations document the failure mode.

irregularities.title: Displayed rank-50 frontier decreased between two same-day captures; the board is corrected, not append-only
irregularities.detail: Between 2026-09-17T16:56:00Z and 2026-09-17T19:04:00Z the displayed rank-50 realized P/L fell from +$1,247,897.00 to +$1,244,313.50 (-$3,583.50), and the exact row value previously at rank 50 (trader rajgaurav009, same percentage and dollars) appeared at rank 49. Realized P/L on closed positions cannot shrink for a still-registered account, so the net effect is exactly one fewer row ahead of it; the most parsimonious explanation is one removal from the public board among rows ranked 1-48 at capture 3 (disqualification or correction). Official rules sections 05, 09 and 16 reserve at-any-time disqualification rights; the official pages publish no board-change log, so removals are only observable indirectly, as here. Capture 5 (20:58Z) then showed the same rank-49/rank-50 rows byte-identical again and the rank-100 boundary pushed down by one new row, i.e. after the single correction the high board was stable for at least 1.9 hours; the frequency of such corrections cannot be measured from the public page.
irregularities.observed: Capture 3 -> capture 4: rank 1 unchanged at +$2,335,125.00; rank 50 -$3,583.50 with the previous row intact one place higher at rank 49; rank 100 +$12,309.65; rank 250 +$2,235.50; participants 95,709 -> 96,095. Capture 4 -> capture 5: rank 1 and rank 50 unchanged to the cent; rank 100 +$2,747.50 with the previous rank-100 row at rank 101; rank 250 +$3,454.50; participants 96,095 -> 96,236.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: A leaderboard frontier is a ratchet: it can only rise as the contest progresses.
irregularities.resolution: Treat every captured frontier as a point-in-time display, never as a guaranteed floor or final threshold. The verifier enforces profit ordering only within a capture, never across captures. Hypothesis H20 records the observation and its test.

irregularities.title: Leaderboard percentage and dollar columns do not always reconcile to the cent within a row
irregularities.detail: The public board displays realized P/L as a two-decimal percentage and as dollars. Re-deriving dollars as 250,000 x percentage / 100 does not always reproduce the displayed dollars: at capture 5, rank 50 displays 497.73% and $1,244,313.50 (re-derived $1,244,325.00, a $11.50 difference) and rank 250 displays 264.30% and $660,759.50 (re-derived $660,750.00, a $9.50 difference), while rank 1 and rank 100 reconcile exactly. The differences are inside the +/- $12.50 bound implied by rounding a longer internal P/L to two percentage decimals, so this is a display-rounding artifact, not a contradiction between sources. It is recorded because the verifier allows the bound rather than exact equality, and a reader comparing the two columns will notice the mismatch.
irregularities.observed: Capture 5 (2026-09-17T20:58:00Z): rank 50 -$11.50 and rank 250 -$9.50 versus the percentage-implied dollars; ranks 1 and 100 exact. Every capture from 1 to 5 stays inside the +/- $12.50 bound.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: The dollar and percentage columns of one row should reconcile exactly.
irregularities.resolution: scripts/verify.py enforces the +/- $12.50 rounding bound on every capture row and never tolerates a larger gap; all displayed values are quoted verbatim in the evidence files and no value is smoothed.

irregularities.title: Intermittent Leaderboard Threshold Acceleration (Surge vs Stasis Dynamics)
irregularities.detail: Leaderboard progression is non-linear and punctuated: after complete frontier stasis across captures 5->6 (20:58Z to 21:27Z), capture 7 (23:08Z) revealed sharp upward threshold acceleration across ranks 50 to 250 in 1.68 hours (Rank 50 rose +$111,303.63, Rank 100 rose +$76,695.00, Rank 250 rose +$38,065.50), while Rank 1 remained unchanged at $2,335,125.00 (+934.05%). Participants rose 96,268 -> 96,344 (+76), demonstrating that leaderboard progression happens in punctuated bursts as participants close batches of winning trades near session closes.
irregularities.observed: Capture 6 to 7 (2026-09-17T21:27:00Z to 2026-09-17T23:08:00Z): Rank 50 rose +$111,303.63 (+44.52 pp), Rank 100 rose +$76,695.00 (+30.68 pp), Rank 250 rose +$38,065.50 (+15.23 pp), while Rank 1 was unchanged. Registered participant count grew +76.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Leaderboard frontiers would advance smoothly or continuously throughout the day.
irregularities.resolution: Record the punctuated surge behavior in data/frontier_history.json and hypotheses (H25), recomputing required daily compound rates from the latest capture.

irregularities.title: Capture CI reported green steps while committing nothing; run logs and artifacts are not readable from the research sandbox
irregularities.detail: Two consecutive intraday capture runs showed every capture step as successful and still left data/intraday/ empty on the branch. Two independent causes: (a) each capture step ran the fetch script and the commit helper in one shell, and GitHub runs that shell with -e, so a non-zero exit from the fetch aborted the step before the commit helper ran - the step then reported success because it was marked continue-on-error; (b) fetch_intraday.py caught only RuntimeError/ValueError/KeyError per series, so a relay answering with an HTML error page (JSONDecodeError) killed the run before the provenance index was written, which meant there was nothing to commit even when the helper did run. Diagnosis was delayed because GitHub serves both run logs and uploaded artifacts from a blob host the sandbox cannot reach, and the checks API exposed no annotations for those runs.
irregularities.observed: Run 35378480898 occupied the single capture concurrency slot for its full 120-minute job timeout inside its 15-minute step and committed nothing; runs 35380931654, 35388315207 and 35388579399 were cancelled while queued behind it; a bounded lane (run 35380480860) completed and uploaded an artifact that also could not be downloaded from the sandbox.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: The brief requires intraday hourly/15-minute ingestion, and the repository treats a committed data/intraday_index.json as the signal that captured bars exist, so a lane that cannot be seen to fail cannot be trusted.
irregularities.resolution: The lane was restructured: fetch and commit are separate steps (the fetch keeps continue-on-error, a failed commit now fails the job); every fetch step tees its output and .github/scripts/capture_diagnostics.py always posts the run's evidence - index presence, per-interval counts, rate-limit state, non-captured series with errors, log tail - as a commit comment readable through the REST API, and writes data/intraday_capture_report.json; the per-series catch in fetch_intraday.py is now broad so one bad payload cannot cost the other series or the index; the intervals run cheapest-and-most-valuable first (daily, hourly, then 15-minute) with explicit --time-budget-seconds caps; concurrency is cancel-in-progress so a superseded run cannot hold the only slot; and commit_capture.sh refuses to commit an index that records zero captured series, because committing one turns a vendor outage into red verifier and derive runs (measured locally: 380 passed / 2 failed instead of 379/0).

irregularities.title: NYSE full-closure table re-verified line by line against official NYSE publications (one date corrected)
irregularities.detail: intel/calendar.py encodes the standing NYSE holiday schedule (nine holidays, weekend observance, Juneteenth from 2022, Gregorian Good Friday) plus two individually recorded special closures (2018-12-05 Bush mourning, 2025-01-09 Carter mourning). It was written in a sandbox with no network access, so no date in it has been checked against the live official calendar yet. Until a networked reviewer completes the protocol in research/evidence/NYSE-CALENDAR-2016-2026.md, the study's calendar_diagnostics must be read as transcription-annotated, not authoritatively calendared; the UTC-date baseline numbers are unaffected either way.
irregularities.observed: 2026-09-19: calendar module added; evidence doc generated from the module (106 closure lines, 2016-2026). 2026-09-19 (later session): all 11 years compared against the official NYSE tables (live nyse.com for 2026-2028; Internet Archive captures of nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars for 2016-2017, 2018-2021, 2021-2023, 2024-2026; ICE press releases for 2018-12-05 and 2025-01-09; Nasdaq Trader 2026 cross-check). One mismatch: 2021-12-31 was wrongly listed as an observed New Year closure - NYSE Rule 7.2 means a Saturday January 1 is not observed (official footnote), and the ENPH daily capture has a 2021-12-31 bar. Fixed in intel/calendar.py nyse-holidays-2; the official transcription now lives in the module and scripts/verify.py fails on any divergence.
irregularities.resolution: Corrected and closed. See research/evidence/NYSE-CALENDAR-2016-2026.md for per-year official URLs and verbatim quotes.

irregularities.title: Official rules page section-09 payment-rails text now reads a 600 USD split vs 1,000 USD at R3-R6
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-19 R10 re-read of the official rules page quotes section 09 as 'Prizes equal to, or more than Six hundred (600) USD will be awarded only via Wire Transfer' and 'Prizes less than Six hundred (600) USD will be awarded via PayPal. No alternative payment methods will be accepted or offered.' The R3-R6 evidence (2026-09-16/17) quotes the same clause as 'Prizes equal to, or more than One thousand (1,000) USD will be awarded only via Wire Transfer or PayPal. Prizes less than One thousand (1,000) USD will be awarded via PayPal only.' Both the threshold (1,000 -> 600) and the large-prize rails ('Wire Transfer or PayPal' -> 'only via Wire Transfer') differ. This may be a genuine mid-competition rules update or a page-render/fetch artifact; the prize ladder, ARV, claim window and all trading constants are unchanged.
irregularities.observed: 2026-09-19 ~18:15-18:45 UTC: R10 chunks 2-3 vs research/evidence/TV-RULES-AMP-SEP2026-R3.md line 62 (and R4-R6).
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Stable payment-rails transcription (1,000 USD split) in data/contest_config.json.
irregularities.resolution: UNRESOLVED: data/contest_config.json keeps the 1,000 USD transcription pending a human re-read of the live rules page. Affects prize logistics only; no trading, ranking, backtest or competition artifact depends on the payment-rails value.

irregularities.title: CME roll-schedule business days come from the NYSE closure table, not a transcribed CME Globex closure set
irregularities.detail: intel/cme_roll.py derives front-contract termination dates from each product's official termination rule, and those rules are expressed in business days (SI: 'the third last business day of the contract month'; CL: '3 business day before the 25th calendar day of the month prior to the contract month'). The only closure table this repository has verified line by line against official publications is the NYSE full-closure table in intel/calendar.py (version nyse-holidays-2, evidence research/evidence/NYSE-CALENDAR-2016-2026.md). CME Globex's own holiday schedule is published per product at https://www.cmegroup.com/trading-hours.html and is not transcribed here, so where a CME closure differs from an NYSE one a derived termination date can be off by one session. The cryptocurrency codecs additionally apply their rule's London-business-day leg as 'not a weekend' because only the U.S. leg is checkable from this repository's calendar.
irregularities.observed: 2026-09-19: data/cme_roll_schedule.json produced 72 dates for 3 of 20 products; every row carries business_day_basis naming the NYSE table, and intel/cme_roll.BUSINESS_DAY_BASIS records the same sentence. scripts/verify.py re-derives every date with the same codecs.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: A roll schedule derived from official CME sources end to end, with the exchange's own closure calendar.
irregularities.resolution: UNRESOLVED but declared: the dependency is recorded on every derived date and in data/cme_roll_schedule.json._meta.declared_limitations, the schedule is not wired into scripts/run_competition.py (so no published result depends on it), and the fix is to transcribe the official CME Globex holiday calendar into intel/calendar.py and re-derive. Until then these dates are research annotations, not execution instructions.

irregularities.title: The derive lane's commit does not re-trigger the verify lane, so main can sit on a stale red build
irregularities.detail: GitHub Actions does not re-trigger workflows from a commit made with the workflow token. When the 'Derive intraday research artifacts' lane commits freshly derived artifacts, the 'Verify research data' run that was already racing the same push keeps its failure (it checked the pre-derive tree, whose artifacts were legitimately stale) and no green successor run is created for the derive commit. main therefore displayed a red verify check on a tree that was in fact in sync.
irregularities.observed: 2026-09-19: run 35465537069 (Verify research data, main, merge commit cca9b0d) failed at 'Re-derive the intraday-dependent artifacts' while run 35465536978 (Derive intraday research artifacts) was concurrently producing commit 11851d0. Re-running the same four builders locally at 11851d0 produced no diff at all, confirming the tree was in sync and only the racing check was stale.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: A CI gate whose colour reflects the committed tree.
irregularities.resolution: MITIGATED: .github/workflows/pages.yml now also triggers on workflow_run completion of the derive lane and checks out github.event.workflow_run.head_sha (fetch-depth 0), so the derived commit gets its own verify run. A red run that was merely racing a derive commit should be re-run rather than read as a defect.

irregularities.title: Official Alpaca IEX bars remain blocked: no repository secrets exist and the automation agent cannot provision them
irregularities.detail: The official-provider lane (.github/workflows/official-bars.yml -> scripts/fetch_official_bars.py) is implemented and fails closed: data/official_bars/availability.json records status 'blocked' (2026-09-18T22:31:46Z, 'Alpaca Basic API credentials unavailable; no network request or fabricated bars'). The lane needs repository secrets APCA_API_KEY_ID / APCA_API_SECRET_KEY. In this session the research agent's token was refused secret management outright (gh secret list -> HTTP 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'), so the agent can neither read nor set the credentials, and the brief's no-fabrication rule forbids inventing them. Every stock figure in the repository therefore stays vendor-tier (Yahoo Finance) until a human account owner adds the two secrets (GitHub -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions) from a free Alpaca account; the lane's daily cron (41 3 * * *) captures automatically afterwards.

irregularities.expected_by_brief: Official Alpaca IEX bars obtained through secure secrets.
irregularities.resolution: Requires human action: create a free Alpaca account, generate an API key pair, add the two secrets listed in research/evidence/ALPACA-OFFICIAL-BARS-ROUTE.md. No agent action can substitute for it.

irregularities.title: CME contract-spec lane answers HTTP 403 from cmegroup.com on GitHub-hosted runners; closed via the agent-fetch lane at 20/20
irregularities.detail: capture-cme-specs.yml transcribes the official contractSpecs page of every pooled future, but cmegroup.com's bot protection returns HTTP 403 Forbidden to GitHub-hosted runner IPs for all 20 products (run 35479263008, 2026-09-20T00:46Z, recorded per record in data/cme_specs_index.json, e.g. 'GET failed with every header set: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/cryptocurrencies/bitcoin/bitcoin/specs (HTTP Error 403: Forbidden)'). The artifact therefore keeps only the three previously audited transcriptions (BTC, ETH, SI) as retained rows and lists the other 17 products in data/cme_product_hours.json _meta.omitted with the exact error text; the roll schedule keeps dates only for products with a transcribed termination rule (BTC/ETH/SI). The lane retries weekly (cron 40 3 * * 1) and on push. Note: a platform page-fetch proxy CAN read these pages (verified 2026-09-20 on the NQ spec page), but it returns a text extraction rather than the raw HTML bytes the verifier re-extracts from, so it cannot feed the byte-verified lane; a manual browser save of the 20 pages (or a residential-IP fetch) would complete it. UPDATE 2026-09-21 (eighteenth pass, re-verified line by line): the direct HTTP lane is still 403-blocked from GitHub-hosted runners (data/cme_specs_index.json records 3 'failed' and 17 'kept_previous' on the last run), but the agent-fetch route (scripts/adopt_agent_fetch.py, raw markdown retained under data/cme_specs/*.agentfetch.md) has since transcribed ALL 20 pooled products. data/cme_product_hours.json now reports product_count 20 with an EMPTY _meta.omitted list, and data/cme_roll_schedule.json carries a committed 196-date roll schedule over 18 coded products (2 documented refusals where no termination codec is justified). The '3/20' figure in the original detail above is therefore superseded and must not be quoted. The direct byte-verified lane remains desirable and keeps retrying weekly; that residual gap is the only part of this irregularity still open.

irregularities.expected_by_brief: Product-specific CME hours and a committed roll schedule for all 20 pooled futures.
irregularities.resolution: Closed for the brief's purposes: product-specific hours (20/20) and a committed roll schedule are both present via the agent-fetch route. Residual: the direct byte-for-byte HTTP transcription lane is still 403-blocked and retries weekly; it is a provenance-tier improvement, not a missing deliverable.

irregularities.title: C24 (H45) and its edition-compatible successor C25 (H46) were both refuted on their first full-pool runs
irregularities.detail: The C24 deep-drawdown volume ignition model was frozen on 2026-09-21 after a fully recorded 36-cell pre-freeze probe (research/strategy/C24-PREFREEZE-PROBE.md) that showed the mean exceeding the median in 34 of 36 cells and 90th-percentile forward returns of 73-143% at a 60-session hold. On the full 20-stock daily pool under the pre-registered decision rule it was nonetheless REFUTED: RuinRiserRoxy -$14,100.70 (48 trades) and LazarusLoretta -$3,332.55 (25 trades) against the B1 control's -$11,803.86. This is logged as an irregularity because the gap between the probe and the competition result is itself informative and must not be quietly dropped: the probe measured unconditional 60-session forward returns from the signal bar, whereas the competition truncates every position at the monthly edition boundary, so a 60-session hold can never complete inside an edition. This was measured, not assumed: intel.competition.EDITION_CALENDAR_DAYS is 30 calendar days, and counting actual captured sessions inside each of the 81 committed daily editions gives min 18, median 21, max 22 sessions - every one of them shorter than the frozen hold_bars of 60, so every C24 position is liquidated by the edition boundary rather than by its own exit rule. The skew the probe found is real in the data but is structurally unreachable under the edition length the official rules impose. No parameter was changed in response; the refutation stands as recorded. FOLLOW-UP 2026-09-21 (same pass, recorded because it changes the conclusion): the structural fix was built and tested. C25 is the identical ignition trigger with hold_bars=15 (< the shortest measured edition of 18), frozen after its own recorded 45-cell short-horizon probe and rostered as SecondWindSybil / PhoenixPhoebe. It was ALSO refuted: SecondWindSybil -$12,655.28 (58 trades) and PhoenixPhoebe -$2,518.00 (34 trades) against the control's -$11,803.86. PhoenixPhoebe did beat the control on the full season but returned $0.00 in the forward held-out split, so it fails the 'both splits' clause of the pre-registered rule. The hold length therefore was NOT the whole story: with the exit now reachable the trigger still does not beat a naive highest-volatility buy-and-hold control. The honest reading is that the probe's positive skew is dominated by a handful of events (AMC 2021, CVNA 2023) that the monthly edition structure and the 50-unit position cap cannot monetise, not that the hold was mis-set.
irregularities.observed: 2026-09-21T22:59:59Z, scripts/assign_full_pool_verdicts.py at 60/60 coverage, 81 season editions, 20 eligible symbols: H45 (C24) -> refuted. Every consumed number is in data/full_pool_verdicts.json. Edition length re-measured 2026-09-21 from the committed TSLA daily capture against the 81 edition windows in data/stock_competition_results.json: min 18 / median 21 / max 22 sessions. | H46 (C25) assigned 'refuted' by the same mechanical rule at the same 60/60 coverage; both verdicts and every consumed number are in data/full_pool_verdicts.json.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: New, unique, high-upside contrarian strategies designed, frozen, tested on real verified pricing and reported honestly whether they win or lose.
irregularities.resolution: Open as a design lesson. Two independent freezes of this trigger family have now been refuted under the pre-registered rule, and NEITHER may be retuned. Before a third attempt, the next session should test the prior question instead: whether the 50-unit-per-instrument cap and the 18-22 session edition make ANY tail-seeking daily model capable of beating the B1 control - the committed official_rule_bound of 4.74x on a single hold suggests the binding constraint is the rule set, not the signal.
